corrected_value.title: Involuntary attentional capture is determined by task set: evidence from event-related brain potentials.

decisions.quote: Previous studies have shown that cues in the target color capture attention, whereas neutral cues do not ( Eimer and Kiss, 2008 ; Lien et al., 2008 ). We hope to replicate this result in the present study.
decisions.reason: No prior adjudication or state file existed for this work. In Experiment 1, the authors explicitly set out to replicate Eimer and Kiss (2008) by testing whether target-color (go) cues elicit an N2pc component and behavioral cueing benefits while neutral cues do not, and they directly compare and confirm this ERP capture finding in the Experiment 1 Results/Discussion and General Discussion. Shipped row 2426 (Anderson & Folk, 2012, 10.3758/s13414-012-0325-9) is a purely behavioral study of go/nogo cueing costs and is a distinct work from Eimer and Kiss (2008) and sibling targets.

decisions.quote: Previous studies have shown that cues in the target color capture attention, whereas neutral cues do not ( Eimer and Kiss, 2008 ; Lien et al., 2008 ). We hope to replicate this result in the present study.
decisions.reason: No prior adjudication or state file existed for this work. Experiment 1 explicitly re-tests the ERP contingent-capture finding of Lien et al. (2008) that target-matching color cues elicit an N2pc and RT cueing benefits whereas neutral cues do not, confirming the result in the Experiment 1 Results/Discussion and General Discussion. Lien et al. (2008) is an independent study distinct from shipped row 2426 (Anderson & Folk, 2012) and from sibling targets Eimer and Kiss (2008) and Eimer et al. (2009).

corrected_value.title: The roles of feature-specific task set and bottom-up salience in attentional capture: an ERP study.

decisions.quote: Previously, Eimer et al. (2009) had observed an enhanced N2 component in response to color-cues that did not match the target cues. Thus, the most straightforward prediction is that an enhanced N2 occurs for neutral and nogo cues alike because both do not match the go-color.
decisions.reason: No prior adjudication or state file existed for this work. Experiment 1 formulates a direct prediction from Eimer et al.'s (2009) spatial-cueing ERP finding of an enhanced anterior N2 to non-matching color cues relative to target-matching color cues, empirically tests cue-related ERPs at Fz for non-matching (neutral and nogo) versus matching (go) cues in Results, and explicitly compares the observed anterior negativity against Eimer et al. (2009) in the Discussion and General Discussion. This 2009 JEP:HPP article is distinct from shipped row 2426 (Anderson & Folk, 2012) and from the 2008 N2pc studies in targets 1 and 2.
